power.answer: Air France allows power banks up to 160 Wh in the cabin only, never in the hold or in the overhead bins. Power banks and spare batteries between 100 and 160 Wh need Air France's approval and are limited to 2 items per person in total.

sections.h: 🔋 What Air France says about power banks
sections.p: From the Air France page "Electric and electronic devices, batteries and replacement batteries", read on 22 November 2026.

head: Question
Air France rule
rows: In the cabin yes, but not in the overhead storage bins; in the hold no
Must stay under your supervision at all times and be readily accessible
Approval is mandatory, requested from Air France or your travel agency before the trip; at most 2 such items per person in total (power banks and spare batteries together)
Each passenger can carry up to 15 battery-powered devices and 20 spare or removed batteries; more needs approval
Each spare battery individually protected against short circuit, ideally in its original packaging, a plastic bag or an individual envelope; cover terminals with non-conductive tape
Must be switched off and their batteries removed and carried in the cabin

list: Not on the page: the section read does not say whether using or charging a power bank on board is banned; ask Air France.

faq: Can I put a power bank in my checked bag on Air France?
No. External batteries must travel in the cabin, not in the hold.
Do I need approval for a large power bank on Air France?
Yes for 100 to 160 Wh: approval must be requested from Air France or your travel agency before you travel.
Can I keep my power bank in the overhead bin on Air France?
No. Power banks are prohibited in the overhead storage bins and must stay accessible.
